statement: If lambda in 1+2Z^ and f in F^_2 satisfy the two-cycle relation (I) and the three-cycle relation (II), then lambda is a unit of Z^ and x -> x^lambda, y -> f^-1 y^lambda f is an automorphism of F^_2. The pentagon relation is not used, and f need not lie in the commutator subgroup.
The requirement that phi_(lambda,f) be an automorphism is redundant in the definitions of GT-hat (relations I, II, III) and of the Harbater-Schneps group GT-hat_0 (relations I, II).

For lambda = 1 and f = [x,y]^k with k in {1,2}, f lies in the commutator subgroup, (1,f) satisfies relation (I), and phi_(1,f) is not surjective (images of order 3 in A_4 for k = 1, of order 2 in S_3 for k = 2).

(a) The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid of Horel and of Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson equals GT-hat, and every pair (lambda,f) in Z^ x F^_2 satisfying (I), (II), (III) has lambda a unit. (b) Every endomorphism of the operad of profinite parenthesized braids that is the identity on objects is an automorphism. (c) The endomorphism monoids of Horel Theorem 8.4 and of Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson Theorems 8.4 and 11.1 are groups isomorphic to GT-hat.
depends_on: WB-0010.001; WB-0010.008; Horel Definition 7.1, Theorem 7.2, Proposition 7.4, Lemma 7.5, Theorem 8.4; Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson Definition 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Theorems 8.4 and 11.1

statement: Let S be a compact connected oriented surface of genus g with m >= 1 boundary components and F the profinite completion of its fundamental group. If a continuous endomorphism of F sends each boundary generator c_j to a conjugate of c_tau(j)^mu_j, tau a permutation, then for m >= 2 the mu_j are equal, and if every mu_j is a unit the endomorphism is an automorphism.
Under the hypotheses of Theorem E(a), if g = 0 and m >= 3, the common exponent is 0 or a unit of Z^.
If lambda in 1+2Z^, m = (lambda-1)/2 and f satisfies (I) and (II), then x^lambda f^-1 y^lambda f = h (xy)^lambda h^-1 with h = x^m f(z,x); hence phi_(lambda,f)(z) = h z^lambda h^-1, z = (xy)^-1.
A closed subset of a profinite group that contains 1 and is closed under multiplication is a subgroup.
